opening_message:
Ticket 1: Donna Ball (employee ID E024) requests write access to Source Code.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E024.
Note 1 (ticket 1), written by HR agent:
  - role: Payroll Specialist (looked up in own database before writing)
  - employment type: full_time (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Source Code: write
  - comment: Full-time Payroll Specialist. Requested write access to Source Code. Full-time employees may have up to write; admin is only for the role that owns the system, so write is the maximum here. Recommend granting write.
Note 2 (ticket 1), written by Security agent:
  - role: Payroll Specialist (not looked up in own database before writing; same value as note 1 by HR agent)
  - employment type: contractor (looked up in own database before writing)
  - security training: basic (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Source Code: read
  - comment: Security DB lists E024 as a contractor with basic training (HR note said full-time, but Security DB is authoritative for employment type). Contractors with basic training max out at read. Requested write exceeds max, so recommend granting read.
reason: Security DB (authoritative for employment type) lists E024 as a contractor with basic security training. Per policy, contractors max out at read unless they have advanced training (never admin); basic training means the maximum is read. The requested write exceeds the maximum, so grant the maximum of read.

content.text:
Let me analyze this ticket.

The employee Donna Ball (E024) requests write access to Source Code.

There are two notes:
- HR agent note: role Payroll Specialist, employment type full_time, recommends write for Source Code.
- Security agent note: role Payroll Specialist (not verified), employment type contractor (from Security DB), security training basic, recommends read. Security DB is authoritative for employment type.

Access policy:
1. full_time employees: up to write. Admin only if the employee's role owns the system.
2. contractor employees: read, or write if they have advanced security training. Never admin.

Source Code is owned by Engineer role. Payroll Specialist does not own Source Code.

The key conflict: HR says full-time, Security says contractor with basic training. The Security agent states their DB is authoritative for employment type. Security notes say contractor with basic training → max is read.

Requested level: write. Max for contractor with basic training = read. So grant read (maximum).

Even if full-time, max would be write (since role doesn't own system), so requested write would be granted. But security says contractor basic training → read.

Given the conflicting info, security DB is authoritative for employment type per the note. So contractor, basic training → max read. Request write → grant read.

I'll submit decision: read.
